doc: NO flag at all: --size defaults to tiles.TILE_SIZE = 1024, --version to v2, --seed to 1, so the script asks build_tile for (1024, 1) and names its files cloud_cell_tiles_1024_v2. A real 1024 bake is too big for a case, so build_tile is replaced by a stand-in that returns the stored 8x8 tile (a fixed byte pattern, arange * 37 mod 256): the sidecar then says size 1024 over an 8x8 tile, which a real bake never does, and the only thing this case checks is the defaults (build_args, the file names and the sidecar fields) plus the encodings of an arbitrary tile. bake_tiles.py is a script: function names its main() (the encodings, not an importable core), run here as __main__ with a __file__ in a temporary folder (its output root) and sys.argv = [bake_tiles.py] + params.argv (the flags are --version, --seed and --size, with the defaults v2, 1 and TILE_SIZE = 1024) and the files it wrote decoded; their compressed bytes are not frozen. Input `tile`: the (size, size, 4) uint8 tile that build_tile returned (data here, not re-derived: raw_channels and build_tile have their own cases). Outputs: rgba = the gunzipped cloud_cell_tiles_<size>_<version>.rgba.gz, RGBA8 rows in order (row 0 first, the tile has no north), 4 bytes a texel in R heaps, G closed, B open, A sheet order = tile.reshape(-1); preview = the 8-bit grey PNG decoded, (4 size, 4 size): one band of `size` rows a channel in CHANNELS order, each band = [the channel rank | the coverage mask at 0.3 | 0.5 | 0.7, as 0 or 255]; sidecar_json = the .json the script writes, as canonical JSON bytes (parsed then re-dumped with sorted keys and separators , and :, ASCII; a port compares the parsed values, the script writes indent 2 and the platform line ending); files = the sorted paths written under the output root, one a line, with / separators (output/tiles/<version>/<stem>.rgba.gz, _preview.png and .json, stem = cloud_cell_tiles_<size>_<version>); build_args = (size, seed) as bake_tiles passed them to build_tile, int64 (2,). Pure byte layout and text: exact.
